name: neuroimaging modalities overview
title: Choosing a neuroimaging modality: different objects need different kinds of resolution (spatial, contrast, temporal); radiography, fluoroscopy and CT use X-rays, ultrasound and MRI do not, and each trades its resolution against cost, availability, invasiveness, radiation and scan length

root.title: Which modality best RESOLVES the object of interest?
lines: SPATIAL: tell apart nearby objects · CONTRAST: tell apart objects of similar density · TEMPORAL: see change over time
